item.title: By: carl
item.dc:creator: carl
item.description:
Ah heck, don't delete. Aren't we always rehashing and rephrasing what has already been said countless times anyway. Especially core 'truths' of which we need to be constantly reminded to help avoid the full-on <a href="https://centertao.local/blog/2011/03/23/he-who-conquers-self/" rel="nofollow">bio-hoodwink</a>.
As far as a "need to have more people thinking like this", this is happening naturally as life expectancy increases. For me, life has been a process of eliminating dead ends... ironically on my way to my dead end. The closer I come, the easier the way.

item.title: By: Bruce McCormick
item.dc:creator: Bruce McCormick
item.description:
Very refreshing and "reassuring" to know that I'm not the only one thinking like this! After WWII, we were the only industrialized country left intact on the planet, so everyone had to buy from use. Thus we had what you referred to as "an era of unusual affluence".
................. I had just written several paragraphs from the perspective of my soap box and realized I was pretty much restating what you had already said, so I deleted them.
I came across your web site while continuing my Daoist studies (go to TheDaodejing.com or put "Daodejing Bruce" in the Google or Amazon.com search boxes) and I look forward to following your commentary. Keep up the good work. We need to have more people thinking like this.

item.title: By: carl
item.dc:creator: carl
item.description:
My father used to refer to futile matters as "pissin in the wind". That frequently applies to voices of reason (especially my brand of reason), so thanks the "Bravo".
This situation sure demonstrates how, like all animals, we take what we can and pay as little (if anything) as possible. It is instinct no different from the gophers chewing away in the field, for example. They eat all they can without concern for pay-back. Hawks flying overhead and snakes slithering on the ground take care of pushing back on a gopher's rapaciousness. What pushes back on our rapaciousness? I suppose we set up institutions like government and religion to handle that. Alas, this is like the fox being in charge of securing the hen house; no wonder these institutions work disappoint.
